text: Extend the existing additive-plus-16-dimensional user/video interaction model with a shared representation and an auxiliary impression-level is_click binary-cross-entropy head, weighting the auxiliary loss at 0.2 while keeping long_view as the sole scored output and preserving the current split, optimizer, and within-user evaluation. This tests whether click supervision improves long-view ordering without changing the fixed ranking objective.
rationale: The current model reaches primary 0.5885 from GAUC 0.6499 and nDCG@5 0.5272, while its high recall (0.773) and lower precision (0.457) suggest imperfect separation. Ranking diagnostics are moderate (MAP@5 0.474, MRR@5 0.533, HitRate@5 0.674), and the score distribution is non-collapsed (mean -0.845, standard deviation 1.108), so an auxiliary click signal could improve representation quality rather than merely rescale scores. The 0.2 weight limits interference with long_view optimization and is feasible with one additional head and shared parameters; validation must select checkpoints and judge success only by primary, with classification and ranking metrics retained for diagnosis.
